situation: A query outside withOrganizationContext()
given: a read of an Organization-owned table on the ranza_app connection, with no request context published
when: the query runs
then: it returns no rows and raises nothing: the policies see a null acting user and deny, which reads as missing data rather than an error. That is why reaching such a table outside the context is a bug (AGENTS.md security invariants, ADR 0001, ADR 0007)
test_name: tenant-isolation.test.ts: denies when no context is set — the pooled connection must not leak; organization_property_foundation.test.sql: without request context no Property is visible; organization_property_foundation.test.sql: without request context no Organization is visible

situation: One pooled connection serves two people in turn
given: Prisma pools connections under the one ranza_app role
when: a request publishes Staff Member A, and the same connection then runs a second user's request or a contextless query
then: each sees only their own Organization and the contextless query sees nothing: the context is transaction-local, so it cannot outlive the transaction that set it (ADR 0001; commit a980f9e)
test_name: tenant-isolation.test.ts: isolates a second user on the same pooled client; tenant-isolation.test.ts: does not leak context into a later contextless query

situation: How the acting user reaches the database
given: withOrganizationContext() is handed a user id
when: it opens the read
then: it validates the id, binds it as a parameter rather than interpolating it, calls app.set_request_context() and runs the query inside that same transaction; a malformed id is refused before the database is reached (commit 3289a6e)
test_name: tenant-context.test.ts: publishes the acting user before running the query; tenant-context.test.ts: binds the user id instead of interpolating it; tenant-context.test.ts: runs the query inside the same transaction that set the context; tenant-context.test.ts: rejects a malformed user id before reaching the database

situation: The runtime role is privileged
given: ranza_app is neither a table owner nor BYPASSRLS, and every table carries FORCE row level security
when: DATABASE_URL is pointed at the owner or a BYPASSRLS role
then: the isolation suite goes red on every assertion, because such a role reads every Organization; queries are never run as a privileged role to make them work (AGENTS.md security invariants, ADR 0001; commit a980f9e, which watched this test fail against the owner)
test_name: tenant-isolation.test.ts: returns only the acting user's Organization

situation: The Workspace or the Portal is started on the migration connection
given: DIRECT_URL is the owner's connection and bypasses every policy
when: DATABASE_URL is set to the same URL
then: the composition root refuses to build. It cannot detect any other privileged role from a URL; the worker asserts its role against pg_roles at boot (ADR 0018), the two request hosts do not. Stated in ADR 0012's consequences; nothing tests either host's refusal — only the worker's

situation: The query path reaching credentials
given: auth_user, auth_session, auth_account, auth_verification, auth_two_factor and auth_rate_limit hold password hashes, session tokens, second factors and counters
when: code on the ranza_app connection selects from any of them
then: permission denied: ranza_auth holds the grants and ranza_app none. RLS is deliberately absent there because authentication happens before an identity is known, so role grants are the boundary (ADR 0005, AGENTS.md security invariants)
test_name: auth-flow.test.ts: denies the tenant query path any access to credentials; two_factor_credentials.test.sql: the tenant query path holds no privilege on password hashes; two_factor_credentials.test.sql: the tenant query path holds no privilege on the TOTP secret

situation: The credential role reaching Organization data
given: ranza_auth has policies scoped to it on public.users and auth_identities, because sign-up needs them under FORCE row level security
when: a defect on the credential connection reads Organization-owned tables
then: it reaches none: ranza_auth holds no grant on any Organization-owned table, so reading every identity row reveals no Organization's data (ADR 0005). Stated, and asserted only for the outbox tables (platform_outbox.test.sql); no suite asserts the absence across public

situation: Gate 1 alone — a lapsed Subscription
given: the Organization's Subscription is suspended or cancelled and gates 2 to 5 are open
when: a Staff Member asks for any capability at any of its Properties
then: denied, and every read gated on it comes back empty (blueprint 3.5; commit 3289a6e)
test_name: organization_property_foundation.test.sql: gate 1 denies when the Subscription is suspended; workspace-access.test.ts: gate 1 — a cancelled Subscription denies

situation: Gate 2 alone — a module not in the Subscription
given: the Organization has no active Entitlement for the module and every other gate is open
when: a Staff Member asks for a capability of that module
then: denied (blueprint 3.5)
test_name: organization_property_foundation.test.sql: gate 2 denies a module the Organization is not entitled to; workspace-access.test.ts: gate 2 — a revoked Entitlement denies

situation: Gate 3 alone — a capability the Property has not enabled
given: the module is entitled, but the Property's property_capabilities row is disabled or absent
when: a Staff Member asks for that capability at that Property
then: denied either way; a disabled row and no row are the same answer (blueprint 3.5, story 2)
test_name: organization_property_foundation.test.sql: gate 3 denies a capability that is not enabled for the Property; organization_property_foundation.test.sql: gate 3 denies a Property with no capability row; workspace-access.test.ts: gate 3 — a capability disabled on the Property denies

situation: Gate 4 alone — a Property the Staff Member does not reach
given: gates 1 to 3 are open at the Property
when: the Staff Member is not assigned to it, belongs to another Organization, or their membership is revoked
then: denied (blueprint 3.5, story 4). What takes reach away and what then happens to sessions is staff-and-permissions' (SP-S1-11, SP-S1-18)
test_name: organization_property_foundation.test.sql: gate 4 denies a Property the Staff Member is not assigned to; organization_property_foundation.test.sql: gate 4 denies across Organizations; workspace-access.test.ts: gate 4 — a revoked membership denies

situation: Gate 5 alone — the row itself
given: another Organization's Property, or an acting user nobody knows
when: it is addressed directly by id
then: no row, not an error: row-level security decides independently of app.can_use_capability(), so a defect in that function still cannot expose another Organization (blueprint 3.5, 7.1, story 26; commit 3289a6e)
test_name: organization_property_foundation.test.sql: another Organization's Property is invisible even when addressed directly; workspace-access.test.ts: gate 5 — an unknown acting user sees nothing, rather than everything

situation: What counts as an active Subscription
given: subscriptions.status is one of trialing, active, past_due, suspended, cancelled
when: the Organization is trialing, or falls past_due
then: trialing admits like active; past_due denies at once, with no grace period. That is app.capability_is_available() today; blueprint 3.5 says only 'an active Subscription', and no ADR or test says which statuses count or whether past_due should lock a front desk out mid-shift

situation: A suspended Organization or a suspended person
given: organizations.status (pending by default, active, suspended, archived) and users.status (active, suspended, archived) exist
when: an Organization or a user is marked suspended while its Subscription and memberships stay active
then: nothing changes: no gate, policy or reach function reads either column, so both are inert. Whether they should deny, and how they differ from a lapsed Subscription or a revoked membership, has never been decided

situation: An archived Property
given: properties.status is archived
when: any Staff Member, organization_wide or assigned, reads or writes there
then: it is out of everybody's reach, because app.accessible_property_ids() admits only active Properties; the audit log still names it (ADR 0031). Code only: no ADR states it for reach and no test asserts the exclusion

situation: Signed in, belonging to no Organization
given: a Ranza user with a valid session and no membership
when: they open any page
then: every read is empty: an identity grants nothing until a membership exists (ADR 0005 implementation notes). How the page explains it is SP-S1-25
test_name: auth-flow.test.ts: sees nothing before a membership exists; auth-flow.test.ts: sees exactly its Organization once a membership is granted; workspace-access.test.ts: shows nothing to a user with no membership

situation: Organization-wide and assigned reach
given: one membership is organization_wide and another assigned_properties with one assignment
when: each reads Properties
then: the first sees every Property of its Organization, the second only the assigned one, and neither sees another Organization's (blueprint story 4, 7.2)
test_name: organization_property_foundation.test.sql: an organization_wide owner sees every Property in their Organization; organization_property_foundation.test.sql: assigned_properties staff see only their assigned Property; workspace-access.test.ts: does not reach a Property in the Organization that was never assigned; workspace-access.test.ts: reaches both once the membership is Organization-wide

situation: A Staff Member of two Organizations
given: active memberships in Organization A and Organization B
when: they read Properties
then: they reach the union of both memberships, and each Property is gated by its own Organization's Subscription and Entitlements; nothing one membership grants reaches the other Organization (blueprint 7.2). No test builds one person with two memberships for this read; AL-S1-04 and the Guest search own their own cases

situation: A Staff Member who is also a Resident
given: a Staff Member assigned to Property 1 has a current Stay at Property 2 of the same Organization
when: the Workspace shell asks which Properties they may use
then: Property 2 is absent: the Stay grants a Resident's reach through its own policies and never widens Staff reach (ADR 0009; found and pinned in PR #58)
test_name: workspace-access.test.ts: keeps out a Property the viewer only stays at

situation: Reaching the database from a page
given: a file under apps/*/src outside src/server/
when: it imports @ranza/db, @ranza/auth, a Ranza module or a platform module
then: the build fails: the session, the subject-to-user mapping and the request context are one funnel in src/server/viewer.ts, and nothing else may reach the database (ADR 0007, ADR 0028)
test_name: dependency-boundaries.mjs: tenant data is reachable only through the server funnel; dependency-boundaries.mjs: the funnel rule covers every Ranza domain module

situation: Signing in maps a provider subject to a Ranza user
given: Better Auth authenticates the person and returns its own subject
when: the viewer is resolved
then: the subject is mapped through auth_identities on (issuer, subject), never on email; the same subject signing in again reuses the same Ranza user; app.current_user_id() only ever returns the Ranza id (ADR 0005)
test_name: auth-flow.test.ts: links the provider subject to a Ranza user; auth-flow.test.ts: does not create a second Ranza user when the same subject signs in again

situation: Two first sign-ins of one subject at once
given: a subject with no Ranza user yet
when: two requests resolve the viewer concurrently
then: one Ranza user results: linkRanzaUser() re-checks inside its transaction and auth_identities is unique on (issuer, subject), so the loser fails rather than creating a second user. Code only; no test races it

situation: Somebody pre-registers an address before its owner is invited
given: sign-up is open (OA-DIFF-02) and requires no email verification; app.identify_staff_user() reuses whatever public.users row matches lower(email); linkRanzaUser() writes the session's unverified email
when: a stranger signs up as someone@their-hotel, opens any page, and that Organization later invites someone@their-hotel
then: read from the code, not run: the invitation attaches an active membership (SP-S1-01) to the Ranza user the stranger's credential maps to. Whether an address must be verified before it names a Ranza user, or invitation must never adopt a user it did not create, has not been decided. Decide with OA-S2-04: linking a new login to an existing user by email, the obvious fix there, is what lets a stranger claim an invited address here

situation: An invited person tries to get in
given: an invitation created a public.users row with no auth_identities row; no route is wired to accept an invitation (SP-S1-32)
when: the invitee signs up with the invited address
then: read from the code, not run: linkRanzaUser() inserts a new public.users row for the new subject, which collides with users_email_lower_idx, so the page errors and the invitee never reaches the membership. ADR 0005 decides the mapping is by subject; how an email-only user gains a subject is undecided. Decide with OA-S2-03, which the obvious fix — link by email — would open

situation: Sign-in fails
given: the Workspace and the Portal sign-in forms
when: Better Auth answers with a mismatch code, a 429, a spent second-factor challenge, a refused origin, a 5xx, or nothing
then: only a mismatch code says the password or code did not match; a 429 says too many attempts; a spent challenge goes back to the password; anything else says signing in is not working and is logged to the console, there being no client error reporter yet (PR #65, F-5)
test_name: sign-in-form.test.tsx: still says it did not match when it did not; sign-in-form.test.tsx: says too many attempts at the second-factor step too; sign-in-form.test.tsx: says signing in is not working when the origin is refused; sign-in-form.test.tsx: says signing in is not working on a server error; sign-in-form.test.tsx: says so, and lets them try again, when there is no answer at all; two-factor.test.ts: answers each mismatch with the code the sign-in forms read

situation: A burst of sign-in attempts across instances
given: Better Auth's built-in rule of three attempts per ten seconds on /sign-in and /two-factor/*
when: attempts are spread across two application instances
then: they count against one limit, because the counter lives in auth_rate_limit rather than process memory; ranza_app cannot reach the counter, since resetting it would switch the limit off (blueprint 7.6; ADR 0010 amendment; commit 85fa2eb)
test_name: rate-limit.test.ts: refuses a burst of sign-in attempts; rate-limit.test.ts: counts a second instance's attempts against the same limit; rate-limit.test.ts: writes the counter where every instance can read it; rate-limit.test.ts: is not reachable from the tenant query path

situation: The rate limiter under load
given: the database-backed counter is written on every sign-in
when: the database is slow
then: sign-in can time out on the limiter itself (PR #58, 'found, not fixed'). Whether a limiter that cannot answer should admit or refuse has not been decided

situation: A session ended while the Workspace is open
given: a Staff Member is on a page and their session ends — a reach change (SP-S4-01), expiry, or deletion
when: they move to another page through the rail
then: that page sends them to sign in: every page calls requireViewer itself, because a client navigation does not re-run the layout; Better Auth's cookieCache stays off so an ended session does not keep working for minutes (PR #58; ADR 0027)
test_name: workspace-pages-gate-the-session.test.ts: each send an ended session to sign in; navigation.spec.ts: a session ended while the workspace is open goes to sign in on the next page

situation: A page built without a session
given: Next.js prerenders any page that reads nothing request-scoped
when: a Workspace page is built
then: it is never prerendered: the viewer reads request headers before touching the composition root, which marks every page beneath it request-scoped (ADR 0007). Stated; no test asserts it

situation: Enrolling a second factor
given: a signed-in person on the Workspace security page
when: they start enrolment and leave, enter a wrong code, or enter the right one
then: the secret is stored unverified and nothing is enabled until a correct code proves the authenticator holds it; a wrong code leaves it disabled; a mis-scanned key costs a retry rather than an account (ADR 0010)
test_name: two-factor.test.ts: hands back a secret and backup codes; two-factor.test.ts: does not enable anything until a code proves the secret was scanned; two-factor.test.ts: refuses a wrong code, and stays disabled; two-factor.test.ts: enables on the first correct code

situation: A second factor belongs to the person
given: the TOTP secret and backup codes
when: anything on the ranza_app connection looks for them
then: they live in auth_two_factor beside the password, with no organization_id and no RLS, reached only by ranza_auth, and never in the clear (ADR 0010)
test_name: two_factor_credentials.test.sql: the tenant query path holds no privilege on the TOTP secret; two_factor_credentials.test.sql: the authentication role reaches the second factor and nothing more; two-factor.test.ts: is unreachable from the tenant query path; two-factor.test.ts: is never stored in the clear

situation: Signing in once a second factor exists
given: an account with a verified second factor
when: the person signs in with the password, then a wrong code, then the right code or a backup code
then: the password alone issues no session; a wrong code is refused; the right code completes; each backup code works once (ADR 0010)
test_name: two-factor.test.ts: stops issuing a session for a password alone; two-factor.test.ts: refuses the challenge with a wrong code; two-factor.test.ts: completes the challenge with the right code; two-factor.test.ts: accepts a backup code, and only once

situation: Guessing a six-digit code
given: a challenge in progress
when: five wrong codes are entered
then: the challenge is burned and its cookie invalidated, so the plugin's lockout columns never engage; a new challenge costs a rate-limited sign-in (OA-S2-06), and the real person signs in again normally (ADR 0010 amendment, PR #65)
test_name: two-factor.test.ts: burns the challenge after a handful of wrong codes; two-factor.test.ts: still lets the real person in after signing in again; sign-in-form.test.tsx: goes back to the password when the challenge is spent

situation: One enrolment, both applications
given: a Staff Member enrolled in the Workspace
when: they sign in to the Portal
then: the Portal's sign-in form handles a second-factor challenge, and both applications' auth modules share one set of Better Auth tables (each calls createAuthModule itself), so an enrolment made in the Workspace is the same enrolment the Portal sees (ADR 0010). The cited tests mock the server; that the Portal's server issues the challenge is not asserted
test_name: sign-in-form.test.tsx (the Guest Portal): says too many attempts at the second-factor step too; sign-in-form.test.tsx (the Guest Portal): goes back to the password when the challenge is spent

situation: Where enrolment lives
given: a Guest or Resident has no account settings surface
when: anybody looks for a place to turn on a second factor
then: only the Workspace offers it, at /{locale}/security, reached from the account menu rather than the rail, because a second factor is not an entitled capability (ADR 0010, commit 17d0e78). No test pins where it is reached from

situation: Migrations and the second factor
given: accounts that existed before the second factor, and an account being removed
when: the migration runs, or the account is deleted
then: no existing account is suddenly required to produce a code, a second-factor row without a secret is unrepresentable, and deleting an account takes its second factor with it (ADR 0010)
test_name: two_factor_credentials.test.sql: an existing account is not suddenly required to produce a second factor; two_factor_credentials.test.sql: a second-factor row without a secret is not representable; two_factor_credentials.test.sql: removing an account takes its second factor with it

situation: No Property named in the URL
given: the viewer reaches several Properties and the URL has no ?property=
when: a Workspace page opens
then: the switcher names the first Property and the page opens on it, so the active Property is always the trigger's label rather than something to open the menu to discover. The first is the first Today Property by Organization name then Property name — code and HK-S1-24, no ADR
test_name: property-switcher.test.tsx: names the first Property when the URL names none; property-switcher.test.tsx: names the Property the URL names; front-desk-property.test.ts: opens on the first Property the viewer may use here when none is named

when: the page opens

given: a Staff Member working at their second Property
when: they click another destination in the rail
then: the Property stays selected; only the switcher changes it (PR #58)
test_name: navigation.spec.ts: the rail moves between pages without a new document, and keeps the Property

situation: Switching Property
given: cached lists for the current Property in the client
when: the Staff Member picks another Property
then: the switch is a full page load, so the client cache is dropped by construction and query keys carry the Organization and Property as a second defence (ADR 0019, PR #58)
test_name: query-keys.test.ts: differs when the Property differs, so a switch cannot be served from cache; query-keys.test.ts: differs when the Organization differs

situation: Is the selection remembered
given: the selection lives only in ?property=
when: the Staff Member signs in again, or opens the Workspace from a bookmark without the parameter
then: it opens on the first Property again: nothing remembers the last choice. Code only; no ADR or PR decides whether it should

situation: One Property only
given: the viewer reaches exactly one Property
when: the page bar renders
then: the Property is named with no menu, since one Property is not a choice; if the URL names another, the lone Property is offered as a choice instead. Code comment only
test_name: property-switcher.test.tsx: names a lone Property without a menu; property-switcher.test.tsx: offers the lone Property as a choice rather than naming it, when the URL names another

situation: Which Properties the switcher lists
given: a Property the viewer reaches for the front desk but whose Today capability is off
when: the switcher opens
then: that Property is absent, because the switcher lists the Today capability's Properties, though other pages can still open on it by URL. Code only; no test and no decision

situation: The rail lists what was bought
given: Properties differ in what is entitled and enabled
when: the shell asks about every destination
then: one read answers each capability exactly as the per-capability gate would, and a destination nobody may use is absent rather than greyed out; hiding it is never the boundary (blueprint 3.5, 4.6; PR #58). A capability withdrawn mid-session stays in the rail until the next full load and its page answers empty
test_name: workspace-access.test.ts: matches the one-at-a-time answers for every viewer; workspace-access.test.ts: keeps the answers apart when they differ; workspace-access.test.ts: answers nothing, for every capability, to a user with no membership

situation: Signing in in Turkish, English or Arabic
given: the sign-in page at /tr, /en or /ar
when: a failure is shown, or the page is Arabic
then: every message reads in that language, and Arabic sets dir=rtl — designed with the feature, not retrofitted (blueprint section 15 rule 7; PR #65)
test_name: sign-in-form.test.tsx: says too many attempts, not a wrong password, on a 429 in tr / en / ar; i18n.test.ts: returns rtl only for Arabic

situation: A Resident reads Stays
given: two Residents at one Property and a Stay in another Organization
when: a Resident reads Stays, or addresses another one directly
then: they see their own Stay and no other, through stays_read_own; the Staff policies are never widened for them (ADR 0009)
test_name: resident_access_path.test.sql: a Resident sees their own Stay and no other; portal-access.test.ts: does not reach another Resident's Stay even when it is addressed directly; portal-access.test.ts: does not reach a Stay in another Organization

situation: A Resident after departure
given: a Stay that has departed
when: the Resident opens the Portal
then: they keep their own Stay record and stop reaching the Property and Unit around it: only a reserved or in_house Stay grants reach (ADR 0009)
test_name: portal-access.test.ts: stops reaching the Property once the Stay has departed; portal-access.test.ts: reaches only the Property and Unit of the Resident's own Stay

situation: A Resident and the Organization's records
given: organizations, organization_memberships, property_assignments, subscriptions, entitlements
when: a Resident reads any of them
then: nothing: gates 1 to 3 are answered on their behalf by app.resident_can_use_capability(), a sibling of the Staff function rather than a condition inside it (ADR 0009)
test_name: resident_access_path.test.sql: a Resident reaches no Organization; resident_access_path.test.sql: a Resident cannot read organization_memberships; resident_access_path.test.sql: a Resident cannot read entitlements; resident_access_path.test.sql: a Resident cannot read subscriptions

situation: A Staff Member in the Portal
given: a Staff Member of the Organization with no Stay
when: they sign in to the Portal
then: they see nothing: a membership grants no Portal reach, and the Portal exposes no staff controls (ADR 0009, blueprint 4.3)
test_name: portal-access.test.ts: shows a Staff Member of the same Organization nothing

situation: The Portal's commercial gates
given: a Resident with a current Stay
when: the Subscription lapses, the Entitlement is revoked, or the Property never enabled the capability — or there is no current Stay
then: the Portal is empty and renders one empty state for all four, deliberately indistinguishable; only the database tests tell them apart (ADR 0009)
test_name: portal-access.test.ts: gate 1 — a suspended Subscription empties the Portal; portal-access.test.ts: gate 2 — a revoked Entitlement empties the Portal; portal-access.test.ts: gate 3 — a capability the Property never enabled empties the Portal; portal-access.test.ts: returns an empty list, not an error, when no Stay is current

situation: A Stay nobody has signed in to
given: stays.user_id is null, as for most Stays Staff create
when: anybody signs in to the Portal
then: that Stay has no Portal, and fails closed twice: a null user_id never matches, and neither does a null acting user (ADR 0009). Stated; no test builds a Stay with no user and asserts the Portal is empty for it

situation: A privileged role without a second factor
given: blueprint 7.6 requires MFA for privileged roles; ADR 0010's amendment records the absence as a known gap against an approved specification, owner at minimum and every Control Plane account
when: an Owner signs in with a password alone
then: they get a session: nothing requires a second factor. The fix is shaped — a check where the session becomes a viewer, not a move of the secret — but it is not built, and the roadmap marks the MFA bullet done

situation: Signing yourself up
given: packages/auth enables email-and-password with sign-up left on, and both apps mount the whole Better Auth handler; the only statement against it is a comment in scripts/db-seed-dev.mjs, which no ADR or blueprint section backs
when: anybody posts to /api/auth/sign-up/email on either application
then: undecided: is public sign-up closed, and must an address be verified before it names a Ranza user? Today an account is created; it reaches nothing (OA-S1-17), but it can pre-empt an invitation (OA-S2-03), and the dev seed and the browser suite depend on the route. Decide together with OA-S2-03 and OA-S2-04

situation: Who decides whether rate limiting is on
given: ADR 0010's amendment and commit 85fa2eb: enforcement is something the host states through AuthDeps.rateLimit, not something inherited from NODE_ENV
when: the Workspace or the Portal composes the auth module
then: neither passes rateLimit, so both fall back to Better Auth's NODE_ENV default — on in a production build, off under pnpm dev — which is the inheritance the decision removed. Only the integration suite states it

situation: Choosing an Organization
given: blueprint 4.6: the shell includes an Organization and Property switcher
when: a Staff Member of two Organizations opens the Property switcher
then: there is no Organization switcher; the one menu lists the Properties of both Organizations under the name of the first one's Organization

situation: Signing out
given: a shared front-desk terminal is named the normal case (query-keys.test.ts), and ADR 0019 clears the client cache on sign-out
when: a Staff Member wants to end their session
then: there is no sign-out control in either application; the account menu holds only the security page. Whether it is simply missing or waits on a decision has not been said

situation: A forgotten password
given: ADR 0005 names recovery among what GoTrue supplied and Better Auth now owns
when: a person cannot remember their password
then: no recovery or change-password flow is wired; like a lost second factor (OA-DEF-01) it is recovered by a database operation today. Not scheduled anywhere

situation: How long a session lasts
given: blueprint 7.6 requires strong session management
when: a session is issued
then: Better Auth's defaults apply — about a week, extended on use — because nothing sets expiresIn or updateAge. No ADR decides the lifetime or an idle timeout for a shared desk

situation: Lost the authenticator and the backup codes
given: a person with a verified second factor and neither device nor codes
when: they ask for access back
then: not now: a reset assisted by Prizic support belongs in the Control Plane with strong authentication, a reason and an immutable audit record (blueprint 4.4). Until then it is a database operation, which ADR 0010 says should not stay true for long

situation: Feature Configuration beyond on or off
given: blueprint 2 defines values at Organization, Property, department or outlet scope
when: an Organization wants a behavioural mode rather than a capability switch
then: not now: only property_capabilities.enabled exists (roadmap Phase 1, 'Entitlements and Feature Configuration: partial')

situation: White-label presentation
given: blueprint 2, 3.1 and 8 specify brand name, logo, colours, domains and terminology
when: an Organization wants its own brand
then: not now: nothing is built (roadmap Phase 1, 'White-label tokens and domains')

situation: Creating Organizations, Subscriptions and Entitlements
